prompts.coreInitial:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original fan-made production sprite sheet for a side-view 2D Metal Gear game. Create exactly 16 distinct hand-authored pixel-art animation phases of PEACE WALKER (BASILISK), from Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker, 1974, in its canonical FOUR-LEGGED battle configuration.
LAYOUT: perfectly regular 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 square cells. Flat pure magenta #FF00FF background. Exactly five thin straight cyan #00FFFF vertical lines and five horizontal lines, including the outside border. No captions or text. Every complete machine fits within its own cell with at least 12% empty magenta clearance on ALL four sides. No effect or limb may touch a guide. Exactly one machine per cell. Same fixed orthographic side view in all cells, facing SCREEN RIGHT; same physical magnification, same limb lengths, same ground baseline. Pixel-art sprites, crisply shaded gray mechanical armor, not a poster or a 3D toy photograph.
IDENTITY LOCK: reproduce the distinctive Peace Walker/Basilisk anatomy shown by the licensed Square Enix Play Arts Kai sculpt and Konami PSP game: elongated articulated central chassis on four jointed industrial legs, two front legs and two rear legs with broad angular armored upper joints, slender segmented lower shins and flat mechanical feet; exposed central cylindrical AI hardware; large dark spherical radome above the fore-body; two very long rectangular dorsal weapons/launch housings mounted side by side above the spine, dark graphite segmented casings with muted burnt-orange end panels; charcoal gray/black steel with subtle rust-orange armored accents and sparse dull-red AI indicator. No human arms, hands, face, cockpit windshield, dinosaur mouth, tracks, wings or tail. NOT ZEKE, REX, RAY, Sahelanthropus, Shagohod or a Gundam. Preserve this one machine in every cell.
ANIMATION ROWS left-to-right, 4 different phases each:
ROW1 IDLE: stable quadrupedal stance, slight joint compression, subtle AI pod/radome sensor adjustment, settling back. Low amplitude but four actually different articulated poses.
ROW2 MOVE: four phases of a real four-legged gait toward the right, contact pose, diagonal legs passing under chassis, opposite contact, opposite legs passing; visibly different bent knees and foot positions, not four copies translated.
ROW3 CHARGE / AIM: plant the four feet, lower and brace front joints slightly, align the existing dorsal weapon housings toward screen right, final sustained aimed ready stance. This is weapon aiming, NOT a physical rush and NOT the nuclear launch story sequence.
ROW4 ATTACK: four successive conventional weapon firing/recoil phases from the existing dorsal weapon assembly pointed right, slight mechanical recoil and recovery across joints; NO long beam, projectile, smoke, explosion or detached effect in this board. Only tiny restrained orange muzzle light if necessary, well inside margins. Do not invent a new gun or transform posture. Conventional combat adaptation, no nuclear detonation.
No scene, ground strip, shadow puddle, user interface, watermarks, labels, logos or branding. The fixed game camera and identical machine identity across all sixteen phases are mandatory.

The large spherical radome and cylindrical AI assembly MUST remain attached and clearly visible throughout all 16 phases, including aiming and launch; they do not vanish or become a cannon. The 2 dorsal missile boxes must remain long, unbroken rectangular structural housings with orange square end caps, same length/scale in every pose. prompts.coreFinalMissileBoxCorrection:

prompts.special:
Use case: identity-preserve. The most recent image is the approved CORE sprite board of Peace Walker/Basilisk. Create its matching SPECIAL board by replacing the actions, while strictly preserving that exact machine design, colors, all proportions, the same 4x4 cyan grid and magenta #FF00FF background, same camera facing SCREEN RIGHT, same physical magnification and bottom-center ground baseline. Exactly sixteen full-machine pixel-art poses, one per cell. The visual size of the machine in neutral poses must equal the top row of the supplied core sheet; do NOT enlarge it to fill the magenta space. Keep the large safe margins (roughly half the cell remains empty). Four real, different articulated phases per action, not scaled or translated copies.
IDENTITY MUST REMAIN EXACT: four industrial articulated legs, angular armored upper joints, feet, long central mechanical chassis, large spherical dark radome at the forward/right end, cylindrical AI hardware underneath, exactly two long rectangular dorsal missile launch boxes with flat muted-orange end caps, dark graphite armor and restrained orange accents. The radome never turns into a head with jaws. Dorsal boxes do not turn into gun barrels. Do not introduce new hardware or extra limbs. No REX/ZEKE parts.
ROW1 RECOVER: phase1 low braced post-launch pose matching core row4, phase2 legs partially straighten and both launcher end caps close, phase3 torso returns near its neutral height, phase4 stable original idle silhouette. Keep same limb lengths; no per-frame resizing.
ROW2 HIT: phase1 machine recoils at the front joints, phase2 knees compress and radome tilts slightly with torso, phase3 rear leg braces to resist shock, phase4 begins righting itself. No white flash overlay, detached sparks or explosion; show actual body articulation.
ROW3 DEATH/DISABLED: phase1 forelegs buckle, phase2 fore-body lowers toward ground as rear legs fold, phase3 chassis collapses low and spherical radome slumps on its mount, phase4 recognizable inert grounded wreck of the same intact machine with all four folded legs and both dorsal boxes still attached, AI indicator dark. Do not merely resize the standing machine. No fire, smoke, explosion, debris or blood. This is a readable gameplay shutdown/collapse adaptation, not the canonical lake ending.
ROW4 SCAN: phase1 neutral idle pose exactly the scale and ground level of core frame0, phase2 cylindrical sensor assembly pans slightly upward while all feet stay planted, phase3 sphere/AI sensor rotates modestly forward/downward on its existing mount, phase4 returns toward neutral. No hologram, beam or HUD scan wedge.
All anatomy and every effect stay entirely within the large safe margins of each cell. No labels, letters, watermark, scene or ground strip. Four columns, four rows, exactly five cyan lines each direction including the outer border.
